{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABYgjUwA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhCE-ps", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 9, "title": "Add side-by-side PMX/glTF Gene Light comparison and fix visible rendering defects", "body": "## Problem

The public [Gene Light glTF demo](https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/) renders successfully, but the converted character looks visibly wrong. Existing tests prove that the GLB is structurally valid, shaders run, and numerical `MMD_materials_toon` fixtures pass; they do **not** establish that the model's geometry, textures, material assignment, or overall appearance match the original PMX.

Add a **side-by-side, directly loaded PMX reference** to the public example, use it to identify and fix clear conversion/loading/rendering defects, and provide reproducible visual evidence for AI-assisted review.

## Expected outcome

At `https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/`, display two clearly labeled views of the **same pinned Gene Light source model**:

| Left: direct PMX reference | Right: MMD glTF |
| --- | --- |
| Load `Gene_light.pmx` and its original images with the `MMDLoader` from [`@takahirox/three-mmd`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader). | Load the converter-generated `model.glb` through the existing `MMD_materials_toon` GLTFLoader plugin. |

The views MUST have matching model pose, framing, scale, camera, light direction, background, and rendering configuration so that differences are actionable. Fix evident defects in the conversion pipeline and/or glTF integration that this comparison reveals.

**The direct PMX view is a practical reference for comparison, not proof that its shaders are bit-identical to the original MikuMikuDance executable.** Document legitimate differences due to the two independently implemented shading models and the extension's current feature scope.

## Context

- Current code: [`examples/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts) renders the generated GLB with toon/PBR switching, but has no original-PMX comparison.
- Converter: [`tools/pmx-to-gltf.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/pmx-to-gltf.ts) outputs **static base-pose geometry**; it intentionally omits bones/skins, animation, IK, physics, morphs, and outlines.
- Original model/reference demo: [`three-mmd-loader` Gene Light example](https://takahirox.github.io/three-mmd-loader/examples/webgl_loader_mmd_pmx_gene.html). That existing demo **animates and simulates physics**; do NOT compare its animated pose directly against the static GLB.
- The reference library uses Three.js r186 and TSL/NodeMaterials. Keep a compatible shared Three.js version rather than introducing duplicate runtime instances.
- Existing tests: [`tests/browser/example.spec.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tests/browser/example.spec.ts) and [`extensions/MMD_materials_toon/tests/`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/tree/main/extensions/MMD_materials_toon/tests).
- Gene Light provenance and rights: [`docs/gene-light.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/gene-light.md), pinned source [`mmdagent-ex/gene` at `c7eace43...`](https://github.com/mmdagent-ex/gene/tree/c7eace43dffaccff6ad0597433ef85fa57c91e03). The model has **CC BY 4.0 and additional use guidelines/trademark-design restrictions**; the public example is a personal noncommercial showcase, not an unrestricted asset grant.

## Implementation guidance

### A. Direct PMX reference in the existing example

1. Integrate `@takahirox/three-mmd` / its `MMDLoader` as a pinned reproducible dependency. Confirm it is installable; if the package is not actually published, use a pinned Git revision or reproducible build instead of inventing an npm release.
2. Use the **same** already-pinned `Gene_light.pmx` and ten image files from the existing hash-verified acquisition process. Extend example packaging to serve the PMX and required textures **only** for this specifically reviewed public comparison; do not add unverified/private models or unrelated full-Gene files.
3. Load the PMX with `MMDLoader.loadAsync`. Compare at **base/rest pose**, with animation, IK stepping, physics and material/UV morphs inactive. Turn reference outlines off for the main apples-to-apples comparison, because the current glTF extension does not implement outlines. Optional outline-on visualization may be separate and explicitly labeled.
4. Ensure both models use the same glTF-compatible world handedness/orientation and **the same effective scale**, accounting for the converter's current `0.08` meters-per-PMX-unit default. Do not alter geometry just to force a screenshot match.
5. Display the two views next to each other on desktop (stacked on narrow screens), with synchronized orbit/zoom and matching camera parameters, fixed sample viewpoints (front, side, back), and consistent rendering backend. A shared renderer with two viewports or another equivalent design is fine. Provide clear loading/error indicators for both models.
6. Preserve the existing option to inspect the glTF's **MMD toon vs core PBR fallback**, without replacing the right pane's primary glTF-toon comparison.

### B. Investigate and fix visibly broken areas

1. Capture comparable **real browser-rendered** images at a fixed viewport and matching pose/camera/light settings, initially using WebGL2 so there is one reproducible backend. Include front and side (and back where informative) captures, not just startup/canvas-color assertions.
2. Inspect the actual paired screenshots, including close-ups as useful. Investigate concrete defects such as missing/wrong material groups, unexpected dark/white regions, wrong texture mapping or V orientation, opacity/blending problems, inverted normals/winding, culling, scale, model positioning, and missing geometry. These are investigation examples, **not** assumed root causes.
3. For each demonstrated defect, trace to the correct layer (PMX parsing/geometry conversion, texture selection, GLB serialization, loader plugin, shader evaluation or scene settings), implement the smallest correct fix, and add a regression check where feasible.
4. Record the **before/after** comparison evidence and short explanations for each meaningful correction in the PR or concise documentation. AI-assisted visual review should actually inspect screenshots, not merely confirm that files exist; describe remaining visible differences and their known reason where possible.
5. Preserve `MMD_materials_toon`'s normative color/math behavior and its numeric conformance tests. **Do not introduce undocumented shader hacks simply to match `three-mmd`**: the reference library and the extension do not use exactly the same shading model. If comparison reveals a probable *specification* error, document it and raise a separately scoped follow-up rather than silently changing the standard.
6. Do not implement general PMX skinning, animation, IK, physics, morph, MMD_outline extension, or a new model format as a workaround.

### C. Public deployment and attribution

- Extend the existing Vite / GitHub Pages build and asset manifest minimally; preserve the `/mmd-gltf/` site base. Keep pinned source checks, and ensure model/image byte hashes and generated derivative provenance are tracked.
- Because the original PMX/images will now be **served publicly** in addition to the converted GLB, verify this is covered by the existing rights review for the same noncommercial purpose. Keep the exact source notices, attribution, usage conditions, and derivative designation prominent and accessible from the comparison page. Do not imply the PMX/GLB is MIT-licensed with the application.
- Update README/example help and applicable documentation so the comparison limitations and local setup are clear.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The built site has **two visible, correctly labeled Gene Light views**: directly loaded original PMX via `@takahirox/three-mmd` and converter-generated GLB via the `MMD_materials_toon` GLTFLoader plugin.
- [ ] Both show the same source/base pose with matching scale, placement, camera, lighting conditions and backend; orbit/zoom stays synchronized. The glTF toon/PBR toggle still works.
- [ ] The direct PMX, original images and required notices are hash-verified and served within the legal/attribution constraints already documented for this personal noncommercial Gene showcase. Build and browser asset loading work without 404, CORS, or shader/runtime failures.
- [ ] Real browser screenshots for matched front/side viewpoints are generated and **visually reviewed** (AI review acceptable); observable major rendering defects are investigated and fixed with before/after evidence and targeted regression coverage. Unresolved or intentional differences are explicitly recorded, not mistaken for success or silently compensated for.
- [ ] Existing independent toon shading/color-space fixture checks, glTF validator checks, TypeScript/tests and browser tests continue passing. Browser integration tests cover both loaders, reference visibility, alignment, synchronized controls, material switch and no console/network errors.
- [ ] Built static preview is checked (not only the Vite dev server); reference PMX/images and notices are included but unnecessary/private upstream assets are excluded. The output remains reproducible from pinned sources.
- [ ] Changes are focused on this comparison/diagnostic goal, its concrete bug fixes, and related tests/docs. No new MMD feature extensions, speculative refactor or silent modification of the normative material equations.

Use existing `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links`, and `git diff --check` as appropriate; record actual results, skips and environment limitations.

## Optional validation

- Capture native WebGPU as well as WebGL2 when an adapter is available; absence of a WebGPU adapter is not a blocker.
- Compare a few additional close-up viewpoints for hair, face and clothing. Do not require pixel-identical output between two different material models.

## Required post-merge verification

After the `main` merge and GitHub Pages deployment, open the **public** `https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/` and verify both models, synchronized navigation, toon/PBR switching, assets/notices and browser console/network are healthy. Record deployment workflow URL, published commit and observed results. These checks occur **after** merge and must not be pre-merge acceptance blockers.
